title: Edge session ghosting and resume patterns notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a scratchpad exploring a lightweight "ghosting" pattern for edge clients to allow interruption, offline periods, and incremental resume of long-lived LLM sessions with minimal server state and predictable cost.

Quick summary:
- Goal: let an edge client drop connectivity (or voluntarily suspend) and later resume a session with bounded work to rebuild local context and KV caches.
- Constraint: hosted serving must avoid holding heavy pinned GPU state for long idle windows. We want a compact resume manifest that captures what the server would need to continue deterministic generation or to reconcile a partial response.
- Target users: mobile/embedded clients, browser kiosks, intermittent networks.

Use-cases:
1) Mobile user starts a long chat, switches airplane mode, then resumes 10m later.
2) Edge device begins a generation job, power-saving mode serializes a minimal ghost, resumes later.
3) Spotty connectivity: server returns partial outputs; client requests resume with previous partial output to dedupe.

Key concepts / vocabulary (working):
- session-id: canonical session namespace (tenant scoped)
- ghost: a lightweight server-side mark saying "this session is suspended; the full runtime has been torn down". Keeps only a resume manifest and some small metadata.
- live-resident: a session with full in-memory KV cache + active runtime.
- resume-manifest: compact payload describing enough to rehydrate, avoid N-token recomputation.
- sentinel: short marker embedded in responses to let client assert they are resuming the same logical stream (helps dedupe).

Failure modes to design for:
- resume-token replay by malicious client (must be scoped + short-lived or signed).
- partial-output duplication when client already has prefix output. Need idempotency keys.
- model-assignment drift: model version pinned in manifest; fallback to compatible variant on mismatch.

API sketches (proposal):
1) Suspend (client or server triggers): POST /v1/sessions/{sid}:suspend
   - body: {"reason":"client-sleep"} or server TTL-based.
   - server returns: {"status":"ghosted","resume_manifest":"<opaque-b64>","ghost_expiry":"2025-02-21T12:00:00Z"} 

2) Resume: POST /v1/sessions/{sid}:resume
   - body: {"resume_manifest":"<opaque-b64>", "client_capabilities": {"kv_cache_preferred":true}}
   - server validates manifest, if valid then either:
     a) hot-resume: reattach to live runtime if it exists OR
     b) rehydrate: allocate runtime and load compact deltas from manifest
   - returns: {"status":"resumed","session_state":"attached|rehydrated","session_token":"<short-signed>","model_variant":"redwood-open-7b-q4"}

Resume-manifest sketch (human-readable form):
{
  "v": 1,                        // manifest version
  "sid": "user-123|session-456",
  "model_id": "redwood-open-7b-q4",
  "sequence_anchor": 2234,     // last server token index
  "prefix_checksums": ["c1a6..."], // rolling checksums of recent prefixes
  "kv_cache_delta_b64": "...", // optional compressed delta for small KV states
  "partial_output_tail": "...", // short tail to help dedupe
  "issued_at": "2025-02-14T10:12:00Z",
  "expires_at": "2025-02-14T10:22:00Z",
  "sig": "base64sig"            // server-signed for replay protection
}

Implementation notes:
- Keep manifest size <= 2KB typical. If KV delta larger, store in short-lived object store and manifest points to signed URL (prefetch cost to rehydrate).
- Allow clients to request a "cheap manifest" (no KV) vs "rich manifest" (kv delta included) depending on battery/network.
- Ghosting TTL policy: short (< 30m) for free tier, reserved/dedicated customers can extend ghost TTLs.

Idempotency and deduplication pattern:
- Responses include sentinel: {"sentinel":"snt-<hash>", "cursor": 2234}
- Client resume request includes last_local_cursor and last_local_sentinel; server compares and trims any overlapping tokens to avoid double-playback.

ASCII diagram (sequence):
Client               Server (runtime)            Object store
  |                      |                           |
  | --- generate() ----> | (tokens T1..Tn streamed)  |
  | gets partial output   |  decide suspend -> ghost  |
  |                      |--- write manifest ------->| (optional)
  |                      |<- return resume_manifest--|
  | (offline)            |                           |
  | (later) resume() --> | (rehydrate from manifest) |
  |                      |-- allocate runtime -------|
  |                      |-- fill kv (optional) ---->|
  |                      |<- resumed token stream ---|

Config knobs (runtime/operator-facing):
- ghost_ttl_default_ms: 600000
- ghost_max_manifest_size_bytes: 2048
- allow_cheap_resumes: true
- kv_delta_storage_backend: s3|gcs|inmemory
- resume_token_signature_algo: ed25519

Edge heuristics (client recommendations):
- Save resume_manifest to secure enclave / OS-keystore if available.
- If resumed and server nacks due to model mismatch, request a "compatibility-roll-forward" route; server should accept a compatible variant and record a small rollback audit.
- When battery low, request "cheap manifest" and accept re-compute on resume.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to integrate with canary rollouts when model variant changes during ghost TTL? (Probably pin variant in manifest and allow admin-configured staleness policy)
- Telemetry: how many resumes pay back vs how many require full recompute? Add counters: resume_hit, resume_miss_recompute, resume_miss_model_mismatch.
- Security: do we need per-tenant revocation list for manifests? Short-lived sigs are simpler.
- UX: client-side monotonic cursor vs token-index; which is easier to expose to SDKs?

Notes to self:
- Prototype flow in serving-runtime: add in-memory "ghost-index" table keyed by (tenant,sid) storing manifest + pointer -> try 2kb manifest limit.
- Add a test harness that simulates intermittent network and measures recompute tokens.
- Pair with Nadia on telemetry dimensions and with Samir on signing library (ed25519).

Snippets to paste into PoC (escaped JSON):

Resume request example (client->server):
{
  "resume_manifest": "eyJ2IjoxLCJzaWQiOiJ1c2VyLTEyM3xzZXNzaW9uLTQ1NiIsIm1vZGVsX2lkIjoicmVkd29vZC1vcGVuLTdiLXE0In0=",
  "last_local_cursor": "2234",
  "client_capabilities": { "kv_cache_preferred": true }
}

Server resume response (happy):
{
  "status": "resumed",
  "session_state": "rehydrated",
  "session_token": "st-A6b...",
  "model_variant": "redwood-open-7b-q4",
  "assigned_node": "node-23"
}

Okay enough for now — this is a working brain dump. Next: convert to tidy API sketch and add linear tickets for tests and telemetry.

-- Maya
